How can you track an emerging virus when infections often go unrecognized? You look at the collective immune memory of over one million plasma donations.

In an Editor’s Choice study published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases, Takeda’s Global Pathogen Safety (GPS) team analyzed U.S. plasma-derived immunoglobulin samples spanning 2006 to 2024.  

What they found was remarkable: A steady rise in antibodies against Bourbon virus. This indicates that the rare tick-borne pathogen may be circulating in the U.S. more widely than documented case numbers reflect.

Because Bourbon virus often causes mild or non-specific symptoms, infections frequently go underreported. Enhanced surveillance of these shifting environmental risks is critical – particularly for people living with immune deficiencies, who face higher risks of severe complications from tick-borne viruses.

Thank you to our GPS team for their continuous innovation and commitment to scientific leadership that helps keep patients and communities safe. 

Explore the full study here: https://lnkd.in/ei_qjYDG

Congratulations to Drs. Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa on receiving the 2026 Lasker Award.

We're proud to congratulate Drs. Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa on receiving the 2026 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award, one of the highest honors in medicine, for their pioneering work uncovering the role of orexin in narcolepsy and opening the door to an entirely new field of sleep-disorder therapies. 

Decades ago, Drs. Mignot and Yanagisawa dedicated themselves to a question few were asking: what actually causes narcolepsy? Their work discovering that narcolepsy type 1 stems from the loss of orexin-producing neurons reshaped the science of sleep and gave researchers a clear biological target where there had once been only mystery.  

That foundational science is what made our breakthroughs in the orexin space possible and has forged a new chapter of care for the estimated 120,000 people in the U.S. (and 2 million people globally) living with narcolepsy type 1. 

Drs. Mignot and Yanagisawa's recognition is a moment of celebration for the entire scientific community and a reminder of why we do this work - to turn bold science into transformative medicines for patients, and to build a healthier world.

Decarbonizing the healthcare ecosystem requires partnerships that drive innovation together. We are proud of our team in Singen, Germany, who have worked with SCHOTT Pharma and Corplex to demonstrate the tangible impact we can achieve together.

We strongly believe that operational sustainability and patient-centered care are deeply connected.

#ClimateAction #HealthcareInnovation #PlanetaryHealth
